name: Carousel
purpose: Coordinate one-active-slide content rotation, optional automatic playback, direct selection, native swipe scrolling, and accessible inactive-slide semantics.
useWhen: A small sequence of authored content should occupy one viewport and support previous, next, direct, touch, or optional timed selection.

avoidWhen.condition: All items should remain visible, named document panels are selected, or a row reveals actions.
avoidWhen.useInstead: ordinary layout or scrolling, Tabs, or SwipeableItem

composition: Compose Root, Viewport, Track, and uniquely valued Slide parts; add Previous, Next, Picker with PickerItem, and RotationControl only when the experience needs those controls.

rules.statement: Provide value or defaultValue matching one Slide and give every Slide a short unique accessible label.
When automatic rotation is enabled, include visible RotationControl, Previous, and Next controls; Picker controls remain optional.
Keep grouped PickerItem controls to a small set because each native picker button is a tab stop.
Supply viewport overflow, one-slide track geometry, and scroll snap in the styled layer; do not replace Atom selection, pause, or inactive semantics.
Do not place essential content only in a slide that users cannot reach without waiting for automatic rotation.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using Tabs for decorative dots, enabling autoplay without a stop control, reusing SwipeableItem, or adding custom timers and aria-hidden logic around Carousel.
commonMistakes.correction: Use Carousel's optional grouped Picker, complete autoplay controls, and Atom-owned state, pause, scrolling, and inactive-slide contract.

validation: Verify controlled and uncontrolled selection, Previous/Next boundaries, loop, picker selection, native touch scrolling, LTR and RTL, and external value changes.

Verify autoplay timing, focus stop without automatic restart, temporary hover and document-visibility pause, visible rotation control, live-region mode, inactive inert state, labels, and reduced-motion handling in the styled layer.
